newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - July 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - High-level authorities not to approve Taiwan governor James Soong's resignation.
Nationalist, Democratic Progressive parties agree to discuss plebscite, presidential election system in next round of constitutional amendments.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - Fifty-eight percent of Taiwan people hope James Soong will stay on (as governor), poll says.
President Lee Teng-hui says whether Soong's resignation will be approved depends on Soong himself.
LIBERTY TIMES - Cabinet to hold James Soong's resignation.
Foreign Ministry will urge Taiwan investors not to invest in Cambodia, if Cambodia insists on closing Taiwan's unofficial trade office.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Taiwan's foreign currency deposits hit new high.
Premier Lien Chan says stock market's seven percent ceiling will be removed gradually.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Chinese communists to tighten monetary policy.
Foreign institutional investors to account for 20 percent of Taiwan stocks within three years.
